## Understanding the Moment Generating Function of the Bernoulli Distribution

This R code provides a comprehensive exploration of the Moment Generating Function (MGF) for the Bernoulli distribution. The script first defines a custom R function, bernoulli_mgf, to calculate the MGF based on the theoretical formula. It then uses this function to numerically approximate the first and second derivatives at t=0, effectively demonstrating how the MGF can be used to derive the distribution's mean and variance. Finally, the code generates two plots using the ggplot2 library. The first plot visualizes the MGF for different probabilities of success (p), while the second plot illustrates a key property: the slope of the MGF at t=0 is equal to the mean of the distribution, providing a strong visual aid for understanding this fundamental concept.

```{r setup}
# ==============================================================================
# R Code for the Moment Generating Function of the Bernoulli Distribution
# ==============================================================================

# This script provides a hands-on demonstration of the MGF for a Bernoulli 
# distribution, showing how it can be used to derive key properties like the 
# mean and variance.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Part 1: Define the MGF Function
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The Moment Generating Function (MGF) for a Bernoulli distribution with 
# parameter 'p' is M(t) = (1-p) + p*e^t.

#' @title Bernoulli Moment Generating Function
#' @description Calculates the MGF for a Bernoulli(p) random variable.
#' @param t The variable of the MGF.
#' @param p The probability of success (between 0 and 1).
#' @return The value of the MGF at time t.
bernoulli_mgf <- function(t, p) {
  # Input validation
  if (p < 0 || p > 1) {
    stop("Probability 'p' must be between 0 and 1.")
  }
  return((1 - p) + p * exp(t))
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Part 2: Demonstrate Derivation of Mean and Variance
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The mean of the distribution is the first derivative of the MGF evaluated at t=0.
# The variance is the second moment minus the square of the mean.
# We will approximate the derivatives using a small value for h.

# Set the probability of success
p <- 0.6

# Set a small value for approximation (approaching zero)
h <- 1e-6

# 1. Calculate the theoretical mean and variance
theoretical_mean <- p
theoretical_variance <- p * (1 - p)

cat("Theoretical Mean:", theoretical_mean, "\n")
cat("Theoretical Variance:", theoretical_variance, "\n\n")

# 2. Approximate the first derivative to find the mean
# Formula for first derivative: f'(x) ≈ (f(x+h) - f(x))/h
mgf_at_h <- bernoulli_mgf(h, p)
mgf_at_0 <- bernoulli_mgf(0, p)
approximated_mean <- (mgf_at_h - mgf_at_0) / h

cat("Approximated Mean (1st Derivative at t=0):", approximated_mean, "\n")

# 3. Approximate the second derivative to find the second moment
# Formula for second derivative: f''(x) ≈ (f(x+h) - 2f(x) + f(x-h))/h^2
mgf_at_minus_h <- bernoulli_mgf(-h, p)
approximated_second_moment <- (mgf_at_h - 2 * mgf_at_0 + mgf_at_minus_h) / h^2

cat("Approximated Second Moment (2nd Derivative at t=0):", approximated_second_moment, "\n")

# 4. Calculate the approximated variance from the moments
approximated_variance <- approximated_second_moment - (approximated_mean)^2

cat("Approximated Variance:", approximated_variance, "\n\n")

# Compare with theoretical values
cat("Comparison:\n")
cat("Mean is close:", isTRUE(all.equal(approximated_mean, theoretical_mean)), "\n")
cat("Variance is close:", isTRUE(all.equal(approximated_variance, theoretical_variance)), "\n")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Part 3: Visualization of the MGF
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# We will use the 'ggplot2' and 'ggrepel' packages for plotting.
# If they are not installed, install them first:
# install.packages("ggplot2")
# install.packages("ggrepel")

# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

# Set up data for plotting different MGFs
t_values <- seq(-2, 2, by = 0.01)
p_values <- c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8)
plot_data <- data.frame(t = numeric(), mgf = numeric(), p = factor())

for (p in p_values) {
  df_temp <- data.frame(t = t_values,
                        mgf = bernoulli_mgf(t_values, p),
                        p = as.factor(p))
  plot_data <- rbind(plot_data, df_temp)
}

# Plot 1: The MGF for different values of p
p1 <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = t, y = mgf, color = p)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("0.2" = "blue", "0.5" = "black", "0.8" = "red")) +
  labs(
    title = "Moment Generating Function of the Bernoulli Distribution",
    subtitle = "The function's shape changes with the probability of success (p).",
    x = expression(italic(t)),
    y = expression(italic(M)[Y](italic(t))),
    color = "p"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        legend.position = "right")

# Plot 2: Illustrate the Mean as the Slope at t=0
# We'll use p = 0.6 for this example.
p_example <- 0.6
mean_example <- p_example
slope_at_0 <- mean_example
intercept_at_0 <- bernoulli_mgf(0, p_example)

# Create a tangent line at t=0
tangent_line_data <- data.frame(t = t_values, 
                                tangent = intercept_at_0 + slope_at_0 * t_values)

# Create data for the main plot
main_plot_data <- data.frame(t = t_values, 
                             mgf = bernoulli_mgf(t_values, p_example))

# Create the plot
p2 <- ggplot(main_plot_data, aes(x = t, y = mgf)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1.2) +
  geom_line(data = tangent_line_data, aes(x = t, y = tangent), linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = 0, y = intercept_at_0), color = "black", size = 3) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(x = 0, y = intercept_at_0, label = paste0("E[Y] = ", round(mean_example, 2))), 
                  nudge_x = 0.5, nudge_y = 0.1) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean as the Slope of the MGF at t=0",
    subtitle = "The slope of the red dashed line equals the mean (p = 0.6).",
    x = expression(italic(t)),
    y = expression(italic(M)[Y](italic(t)))
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

# Print the plots
print(p1)
print(p2)
```
